scope: Search for research at the intersection of (1) user next-item/sequential behavior, (2) hyperbolic geometry, and (3) generative semantic IDs. Evidence labels indicate the evidence level actually inspected here, not merely whether a PDF URL exists.

sources.title: Recommender Systems with Generative Retrieval

overlap.user_next_item_behavior: ABSTRACT — frames recommendation as generative retrieval and uses user interaction sequences / next-item recommendation settings.
overlap.hyperbolic_geometry: UNKNOWN — no full-text verification of hyperbolic geometry; not indicated by indexed abstract.
overlap.generative_semantic_ids: ABSTRACT — introduces semantic IDs for items and autoregressive generation of IDs.

sources.assessment: Strong two-way neighbor (behavior + generative semantic IDs), not verified as hyperbolic.

sources.title: Hyperbolic Hypergraphs for Sequential Recommendation

overlap.user_next_item_behavior: ABSTRACT — sequential recommendation models user-item interaction histories.
overlap.hyperbolic_geometry: ABSTRACT — hyperbolic hypergraph representation is central to the method.
overlap.generative_semantic_ids: UNKNOWN — no semantic-ID generation indicated in the indexed abstract.

sources.assessment: Strong two-way neighbor (sequential behavior + hyperbolic geometry), not verified as generative semantic-ID work.

sources.title: Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendations with Hyperbolic Representations

overlap.user_next_item_behavior: ABSTRACT — sequential recommendation from user interaction sequences.
overlap.hyperbolic_geometry: ABSTRACT — uses hyperbolic representations in self-attentive sequential recommendation.
overlap.generative_semantic_ids: UNKNOWN — indexed abstract does not establish generative semantic IDs.

sources.assessment: Additional two-way neighbor (behavior + hyperbolic geometry); not an established triple-overlap source.

sources.title: HMamba: Hyperbolic Mamba for Sequential Recommendation

overlap.user_next_item_behavior: ABSTRACT — sequential recommendation from behavior sequences.
overlap.generative_semantic_ids: UNKNOWN — semantic-ID generation is not established by the abstract.

sources.assessment: Recent two-way neighbor (behavior + hyperbolic sequence modeling); no verified semantic-ID component.

behavior_problem_candidates.candidate: Representing user preference evolution and next-item transitions in a hierarchy-aware latent space, then decoding candidate item semantic IDs autoregressively.
behavior_problem_candidates.motivation: The generative-retrieval line establishes semantic-ID generation over interaction sequences; hyperbolic sequential recommenders establish hyperbolic sequence representations. The combination itself is a research gap hypothesis, not a verified prior method.

behavior_problem_candidates.candidate: Test whether hyperbolic distances improve next-item prediction for users with sparse histories or multi-level interests, while retaining semantic-ID generation as the item-output interface.
behavior_problem_candidates.motivation: A plausible behavior-focused evaluation question linking hierarchy-sensitive geometry to sequence-conditioned generative retrieval; the reviewed records do not establish this exact experiment.

limitations: No independently verified paper was found in this search that establishes all three components together; do not describe the intersection as an existing method on this evidence.

Evidence labels are conservative: abstracts and bibliographic metadata were cross-checked via OpenAlex records; full texts were not successfully text-inspected in this run. A PDF URL alone does not qualify as FULL_TEXT evidence.
The search is a targeted discovery search rather than a systematic review; terminology varies (generative retrieval, semantic IDs, sequential recommendation, hyperbolic representation).
UNKNOWN means the accessible evidence did not establish the component, not proof that the full paper lacks it. Check full text before making a definitive negative claim.
The two behavior_problem_candidates are derived research directions, not claims of novelty or verified empirical findings.
